concepts.name: Propositional logic
concepts.summary: Reasoning with statements that are true or false, combined with and, or, not and implies. The bedrock rules every proof relies on.

concepts.name: First-order logic
concepts.summary: Logic extended with variables and the quantifiers 'for all' and 'there exists'. The formal language in which almost all of mathematics can be written.

concepts.name: Mathematical proof
concepts.summary: A chain of logical steps from accepted axioms to a conclusion. Direct proof, contradiction and contrapositive are the everyday techniques.

concepts.name: Sets (ZFC axioms)
concepts.summary: Collections of objects, governed by the Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms. Nearly every mathematical object can be built out of sets.

concepts.name: Ordered pairs & Cartesian products
concepts.summary: Pairs (a, b) where order matters, and the set A × B of all such pairs. The raw material for relations, functions and coordinates.

concepts.name: Relations
concepts.summary: A relation is a set of ordered pairs saying which elements are related, such as 'less than' or 'divides'.

concepts.name: Functions
concepts.summary: A rule assigning each input exactly one output. Injective, surjective and bijective functions let us compare sets.

concepts.name: Equivalence relations
concepts.summary: Relations that are reflexive, symmetric and transitive. They split a set into classes of 'equal for our purposes' elements.

concepts.name: Orders
concepts.summary: Relations like ≤ that let us compare elements. Partial, total and well-orders are the main varieties.

concepts.name: Cardinality
concepts.summary: The size of a set, measured by bijections. Two sets have the same cardinality if their elements can be paired off exactly.

concepts.name: Countable and uncountable sets
concepts.summary: Some infinities are bigger than others. Cantor's diagonal argument shows the real numbers cannot be listed one by one.

concepts.name: Axiom of choice
concepts.summary: From any collection of non-empty sets you can choose one element from each. Independent of the other axioms, and surprisingly powerful.

concepts.name: Zorn's lemma
concepts.summary: If every chain in a partial order has an upper bound, there is a maximal element. Used to prove every vector space has a basis.

concepts.name: Ordinal numbers
concepts.summary: Numbers that extend counting past infinity: ω, ω+1, ω·2 and beyond. They measure the length of well-ordered sequences.

concepts.name: Computability & Turing machines
concepts.summary: A precise model of what an algorithm is. Turing machines capture exactly the functions that can be mechanically computed.

concepts.name: The halting problem
concepts.summary: No algorithm can decide, for every program and input, whether the program eventually stops. The first proof of a fundamental limit on computation.

concepts.name: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
concepts.summary: Any consistent formal system strong enough for arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove, and cannot prove its own consistency.

concepts.name: Model theory
concepts.summary: The study of mathematical structures that satisfy a given set of axioms, and of what logic can and cannot distinguish between them.

concepts.name: Computational complexity (P vs NP)
concepts.summary: Classifying problems by how much time or memory they need. Whether P equals NP is one of the great open problems.

concepts.name: Continuum hypothesis
concepts.summary: Cantor's question: is there an infinity strictly between the whole numbers and the real numbers?

concepts.name: Forcing & independence
concepts.summary: Cohen's method for building new models of set theory. It showed the continuum hypothesis can be neither proved nor disproved from the usual axioms.

concepts.name: Large cardinals
concepts.summary: Infinities so large their existence cannot be proved from ZFC. They form a ladder measuring the strength of mathematical theories.

concepts.name: Homotopy type theory
concepts.summary: A foundation for mathematics where equality behaves like a path between points, designed so proofs can be checked by computer.

concepts.name: Natural numbers (Peano axioms)
concepts.summary: 0, 1, 2, 3, … defined by a starting point and a successor operation. Everything about counting follows from five axioms.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.summary: Prove a statement for 0, then show each case implies the next, and it holds for every natural number. Like toppling an infinite row of dominoes.

concepts.name: Integers
concepts.summary: The whole numbers with negatives, …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …, built so that subtraction always has an answer.

concepts.name: Rational numbers
concepts.summary: Fractions p/q, built so that division by non-zero numbers always has an answer.

concepts.name: Real numbers
concepts.summary: The continuum of the number line, filling the gaps in the rationals (such as √2). Constructed with Dedekind cuts or Cauchy sequences.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.summary: Numbers a + bi where i² = −1. Every polynomial equation has a solution among them.

concepts.name: Quaternions
concepts.summary: A four-dimensional number system where multiplication is not commutative. Widely used to describe 3D rotations.

concepts.name: p-adic numbers
concepts.summary: An alternative completion of the rationals where numbers are close when their difference is divisible by a high power of a prime p.

concepts.name: Divisibility & primes
concepts.summary: When one integer divides another, and the primes: numbers greater than 1 divisible only by 1 and themselves.

concepts.name: Euclidean algorithm
concepts.summary: A fast method for the greatest common divisor of two numbers, by repeated division with remainder. One of the oldest algorithms still in use.

concepts.name: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic
concepts.summary: Every integer greater than 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, up to order.

concepts.name: Infinitely many primes
concepts.summary: Euclid's proof: multiply any finite list of primes together and add 1, and the result has a prime factor missing from the list.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.summary: Clock arithmetic: working with remainders after division by a fixed number n.

concepts.name: Fermat's little theorem
concepts.summary: If p is prime and a is not a multiple of p, then a^(p−1) leaves remainder 1 when divided by p.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.summary: Remainders modulo coprime numbers can be chosen independently, and they pin down a unique number modulo the product.

concepts.name: Quadratic reciprocity
concepts.summary: Gauss's 'golden theorem' linking whether p is a square modulo q to whether q is a square modulo p.

concepts.name: Diophantine equations
concepts.summary: Polynomial equations where only whole-number solutions count, such as x² + y² = z².

concepts.name: Public-key cryptography (RSA)
concepts.summary: Encryption whose security rests on factoring large numbers being hard. The arithmetic behind secure connections on the internet.

concepts.name: Riemann zeta function
concepts.summary: ζ(s) = 1 + 1/2^s + 1/3^s + …, extended to the complex plane. Its behaviour encodes the distribution of the primes.

concepts.name: Prime number theorem
concepts.summary: The number of primes up to x is roughly x / ln x. Proved in 1896 using complex analysis.

concepts.name: Riemann hypothesis
concepts.summary: Open problem: all non-trivial zeros of the zeta function lie on the line Re(s) = ½. It would give the sharpest control over the primes.

concepts.name: Algebraic number theory
concepts.summary: Studies number systems like ℤ[√−5] where unique factorisation can fail, and how ideals restore it.

concepts.name: Elliptic curves
concepts.summary: Curves y² = x³ + ax + b whose points form a group. Central to modern number theory and to cryptography.

concepts.name: Modular forms
concepts.summary: Highly symmetric functions on the complex upper half-plane whose coefficients carry deep arithmetic information.

concepts.name: Fermat's Last Theorem
concepts.summary: xⁿ + yⁿ = zⁿ has no positive whole-number solutions for n > 2. Stated in 1637, proved by Andrew Wiles in 1995.

concepts.name: Dirichlet L-functions
concepts.summary: Relatives of the zeta function that track primes in each remainder class. They prove there are infinitely many primes ending in 7.

concepts.name: Generalised Riemann hypothesis
concepts.summary: Open problem: the zeros of every L-function, not only zeta, lie on the critical line. Many results are proved assuming it.

concepts.name: Montgomery's pair correlation
concepts.summary: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, zeta zeros repel each other exactly like eigenvalues of large random matrices. A striking link between primes and quantum physics.

concepts.name: Adèles & idèles
concepts.summary: A single space that bundles the real numbers with every p-adic completion, so all primes can be handled at once.

concepts.name: Class field theory
concepts.summary: Describes every field extension with an abelian Galois group using only data inside the base field. The abelian case of Langlands.

concepts.name: Galois representations
concepts.summary: Studying the symmetries of all algebraic numbers through how they act on vector spaces, often built from the cohomology of varieties.

concepts.name: Automorphic forms
concepts.summary: The far-reaching generalisation of modular forms to other symmetry groups, studied through representation theory.

concepts.name: Modularity theorem
concepts.summary: Every elliptic curve over the rationals comes from a modular form. Wiles proved enough of it to settle Fermat's Last Theorem.

concepts.name: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
concepts.summary: Open Millennium Prize problem: the number of rational points on an elliptic curve is read off from its L-function at s = 1.

concepts.name: Sato–Tate theorem
concepts.summary: Counting points on an elliptic curve modulo each prime gives errors that follow a precise semicircle-like distribution. Proved in 2011.

concepts.name: Langlands program
concepts.summary: A web of conjectures linking Galois representations with automorphic forms, often called a grand unified theory of mathematics.

concepts.name: Geometric Langlands conjecture
concepts.summary: The Langlands correspondence recast for curves and sheaves. Its proof, announced in 2024, runs to nearly a thousand pages.

concepts.name: Perfectoid spaces
concepts.summary: Scholze's spaces that transfer problems between p-adic numbers and characteristic p, where they become easier.

concepts.name: Green–Tao theorem
concepts.summary: The primes contain arithmetic progressions of every length, such as 3, 5, 7 or 5, 11, 17, 23, 29.

concepts.name: Galois cohomology
concepts.summary: Cohomology of Galois groups. It measures the obstructions to solving equations over a field and controls how Galois representations can vary.

concepts.name: Galois deformation theory
concepts.summary: Mazur's theory of all the ways a Galois representation can be perturbed, packaged into a single universal ring R.

concepts.name: Hecke algebras
concepts.summary: Rings of symmetry operators acting on modular forms. Their eigenvalues carry the arithmetic information inside each form.

concepts.name: Ribet's level-lowering theorem
concepts.summary: Showed that a solution to Fermat's equation would give an elliptic curve that cannot be modular, reducing Fermat to the modularity theorem.

concepts.name: R = T (Taylor–Wiles)
concepts.summary: The heart of Wiles's proof: the universal deformation ring R equals the Hecke algebra T, so every suitable Galois representation comes from a modular form.

concepts.name: p-adic Hodge theory
concepts.summary: Compares étale and de Rham cohomology of p-adic varieties using Fontaine's period rings, classifying p-adic Galois representations.

concepts.name: Diamonds
concepts.summary: Scholze's p-adic spaces glued from perfectoid pieces, flexible enough to build objects with no classical construction.

concepts.name: Fargues–Fontaine curve
concepts.summary: A strange curve that serves as the fundamental curve of p-adic Hodge theory. Vector bundles on it classify p-adic period data.

concepts.name: Fargues–Scholze local Langlands
concepts.summary: A 2021 construction of the local Langlands correspondence by doing geometric Langlands on the Fargues–Fontaine curve.

concepts.name: Arthur–Selberg trace formula
concepts.summary: Equates a spectral sum over automorphic representations with a geometric sum over conjugacy classes. The main tool for comparing automorphic forms on different groups.

concepts.name: Cyclic base change
concepts.summary: Langlands, Arthur and Clozel: automorphic forms can be transferred up cyclic extensions of number fields, proved by comparing trace formulas.

concepts.name: Langlands–Tunnell theorem
concepts.summary: Two-dimensional Galois representations with solvable image are modular. It gave Wiles the starting point his argument then propagates.

concepts.name: Shimura varieties
concepts.summary: Higher-dimensional generalisations of modular curves whose cohomology realises the Langlands correspondence.

concepts.name: Local Langlands for GLₙ (Harris–Taylor)
concepts.summary: The 2001 proof of the local Langlands correspondence for GLₙ, read off from the cohomology of Shimura varieties.

concepts.name: Modularity lifting theorems
concepts.summary: Kisin's and others' extensions of Taylor–Wiles: if a Galois representation is modular modulo p, it is modular.

concepts.name: Serre's modularity conjecture
concepts.summary: Every odd irreducible two-dimensional mod p Galois representation comes from a modular form. Proved by Khare and Wintenberger in 2009.

concepts.name: Potential automorphy
concepts.summary: Taylor's method: show a Galois representation becomes automorphic after a field extension, which is often enough for applications.

concepts.name: Symmetric power functoriality
concepts.summary: Newton and Thorne (2021): all symmetric powers of a modular form's Galois representation are automorphic, a long-sought case of Langlands functoriality.

concepts.name: Galois representations for torsion classes
concepts.summary: Scholze (2015) attached Galois representations to torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric spaces, using perfectoid Shimura varieties.

concepts.name: Potential modularity over CM fields
concepts.summary: The 2018 'ten author' paper proved modularity lifting over CM fields, giving potential modularity of elliptic curves and Ramanujan for Bianchi forms.

concepts.name: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields
concepts.summary: Caraiani and Newton (2023): a positive proportion of elliptic curves over fields like ℚ(i) are modular, building on the ten-author lifting theorems.

concepts.name: Fargues–Scholze meets Harris–Taylor
concepts.summary: Hansen, Kaletha and Weinstein (2022) showed the Fargues–Scholze parameters agree with the classical correspondence for GLₙ and its inner forms.

concepts.name: Binary operations
concepts.summary: A rule combining two elements into one, like addition or composition. Associativity and commutativity are the key properties.

concepts.name: Groups
concepts.summary: A set with an associative operation, an identity and inverses. The language of symmetry.

concepts.name: Subgroups & cosets
concepts.summary: Groups sitting inside larger groups, and the cosets that partition the larger group into equal-sized pieces.

concepts.name: Lagrange's theorem
concepts.summary: In a finite group, the size of every subgroup divides the size of the group.

concepts.name: Permutations & symmetric groups
concepts.summary: All the ways to rearrange n objects form a group, Sₙ. Every finite group lives inside one (Cayley's theorem).

concepts.name: Homomorphisms
concepts.summary: Maps between structures that respect the operations. Isomorphisms show when two structures are really the same.

concepts.name: Normal subgroups & quotient groups
concepts.summary: Collapsing a group by a normal subgroup gives a new, smaller group, the way the integers collapse to clock arithmetic.

concepts.name: Isomorphism theorems
concepts.summary: The image of a homomorphism is the quotient by its kernel, plus two companion results on how subgroups and quotients interact.

concepts.name: Group actions
concepts.summary: A group acting as symmetries of a set. Orbits and stabilisers turn symmetry into counting.

concepts.name: Sylow theorems
concepts.summary: Guarantee subgroups of prime-power size in any finite group, and control how many there are.

concepts.name: Finitely generated abelian groups
concepts.summary: Every such group is a product of copies of ℤ and cyclic groups. A complete classification.

concepts.name: Classification of finite simple groups
concepts.summary: The 'atoms' of finite groups: cyclic, alternating, Lie type, and 26 sporadic groups, the largest being the Monster.

concepts.name: Rings
concepts.summary: Structures with addition and multiplication, like the integers or polynomials, where division may not be possible.

concepts.name: Ideals & quotient rings
concepts.summary: Ideals are the subsets you can quotient a ring by. They generalise 'multiples of n' and power algebraic geometry.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.summary: Expressions like 3x² − 2x + 1, forming a ring of their own. Their roots drive much of algebra.

concepts.name: Fields
concepts.summary: Rings where every non-zero element can be divided by, like the rationals, reals and complex numbers.

concepts.name: Finite fields
concepts.summary: Fields with finitely many elements, which exist exactly for prime-power sizes. Used in coding theory and cryptography.

concepts.name: Field extensions
concepts.summary: Bigger fields built by adjoining roots of polynomials, like ℚ(√2). Their degree is a dimension.

concepts.name: Galois theory
concepts.summary: Matches field extensions with groups of symmetries of their roots, turning questions about equations into questions about groups.

concepts.name: Insolvability of the quintic
concepts.summary: There is no formula using only arithmetic and roots that solves every degree-5 polynomial equation (Abel–Ruffini).

concepts.name: Ruler-and-compass constructions
concepts.summary: Shows why trisecting an angle and doubling the cube are impossible with straightedge and compass alone.

concepts.name: Fundamental theorem of algebra
concepts.summary: Every non-constant polynomial has a root in the complex numbers.

concepts.name: Modules
concepts.summary: Vector spaces where the scalars come from a ring instead of a field. They unify abelian groups and linear algebra.

concepts.name: Representation theory
concepts.summary: Studying groups by letting them act as matrices. Character tables reveal a group's structure.

concepts.name: Categories & functors
concepts.summary: An abstract language of objects and arrows that captures what different branches of mathematics have in common.

concepts.name: Yoneda lemma
concepts.summary: An object is completely determined by how other objects map into it. A cornerstone of category theory.

concepts.name: Homological algebra
concepts.summary: Chain complexes, exact sequences and derived functors: machinery for measuring how far constructions fail to be exact.

concepts.name: Lie groups
concepts.summary: Groups that are also smooth spaces, like the rotations of 3D space. The mathematics of continuous symmetry.

concepts.name: Lie algebras
concepts.summary: The linearised, infinitesimal version of a Lie group. Their classification underlies particle physics.

concepts.name: Spectral sequences
concepts.summary: A bookkeeping machine that computes complicated (co)homology one approximation, or 'page', at a time.

concepts.name: Derived categories
concepts.summary: A setting where chain complexes themselves become the objects, so constructions only need to be correct up to homology.

concepts.name: ∞-categories
concepts.summary: Categories where arrows between arrows, and so on forever, are part of the structure. The language of modern homotopy theory.

concepts.name: Condensed mathematics
concepts.summary: Clausen and Scholze's replacement for topological spaces that makes algebra and analysis fit together cleanly.

concepts.name: Reductive algebraic groups
concepts.summary: Groups like GLₙ defined by polynomial equations, which make sense over any field. The symmetry groups of the Langlands program.

concepts.name: Vector spaces
concepts.summary: Sets of vectors you can add and scale. The setting for everything linear, from arrows in the plane to spaces of functions.

concepts.name: Basis & dimension
concepts.summary: A minimal set of vectors from which every vector is uniquely built. Its size, the dimension, is the same for every basis.

concepts.name: Linear maps
concepts.summary: Functions that respect addition and scaling. Rotations, projections and derivatives are all examples.

concepts.name: Matrices
concepts.summary: Grids of numbers representing linear maps once a basis is fixed. Matrix multiplication is composition of maps.

concepts.name: Systems of linear equations
concepts.summary: Solving many linear equations at once with Gaussian elimination. Rank tells you how many solutions exist.

concepts.name: Determinants
concepts.summary: A single number measuring how a linear map scales volume. Zero exactly when the map cannot be undone.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues & eigenvectors
concepts.summary: Directions a linear map only stretches, and by how much. They reveal the essential behaviour of the map.

concepts.name: Jordan normal form
concepts.summary: Every complex matrix is similar to an almost-diagonal one built from simple blocks.

concepts.name: Inner products & orthogonality
concepts.summary: Adds lengths and angles to a vector space through a dot product. Orthogonal projection is its workhorse.

concepts.name: Spectral theorem
concepts.summary: Symmetric matrices can be diagonalised by a rotation: they simply stretch along perpendicular axes.

concepts.name: Singular value decomposition
concepts.summary: Any matrix is a rotation, a stretch, and another rotation. The basis of data compression and principal component analysis.

concepts.name: Dual spaces
concepts.summary: The space of linear functions from a vector space to its scalars. Measuring a vector instead of describing it.

concepts.name: Tensors
concepts.summary: Multilinear objects combining several vectors and covectors, used for stress, curvature and quantum states.

concepts.name: Limits of sequences
concepts.summary: What it means for a sequence to approach a value, made precise with ε and N.

concepts.name: Infinite series
concepts.summary: Adding infinitely many numbers. Convergence tests tell whether the sum settles to a finite value.

concepts.name: Continuity
concepts.summary: A function is continuous if small changes in input give small changes in output: no jumps or tears.

concepts.name: Intermediate value theorem
concepts.summary: A continuous function that goes from below zero to above zero must cross zero somewhere in between.

concepts.name: Extreme value theorem
concepts.summary: A continuous function on a closed, bounded interval reaches a maximum and a minimum.

concepts.name: Derivatives
concepts.summary: The instantaneous rate of change of a function: the slope of its tangent line.

concepts.name: Mean value theorem
concepts.summary: Somewhere along a smooth curve, the slope equals the average slope between the endpoints.

concepts.name: Integrals
concepts.summary: Area under a curve, defined as the limit of sums of thin rectangles.

concepts.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
concepts.summary: Differentiation and integration undo each other, so areas can be computed with antiderivatives.

concepts.name: Exponentials & logarithms
concepts.summary: eˣ is the function equal to its own derivative, and ln x is its inverse. The language of growth and decay.

concepts.name: Trigonometric functions
concepts.summary: Sine, cosine and tangent relate angles to lengths, and describe anything that oscillates.

concepts.name: Euler's formula
concepts.summary: e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ, tying exponentials to rotation. At θ = π it gives e^(iπ) + 1 = 0.

concepts.name: Taylor series
concepts.summary: Writing a function as an infinite polynomial built from its derivatives at a single point.

concepts.name: Uniform convergence
concepts.summary: Convergence of functions that is equally good everywhere, which is what lets limits, integrals and derivatives be swapped.

concepts.name: Multivariable calculus
concepts.summary: Calculus in several dimensions: partial derivatives, gradients, and integrals over regions.

concepts.name: Vector calculus (Green, Stokes, Gauss)
concepts.summary: Integrating a field's derivative over a region equals integrating the field over its boundary. Electromagnetism is written in this language.

concepts.name: Contraction mapping theorem
concepts.summary: A map that brings points closer together on a complete space has exactly one fixed point, found by iterating.

concepts.name: Measure theory
concepts.summary: A rigorous way to assign length, area or volume to very general sets, and the reason some sets cannot be measured.

concepts.name: Lebesgue integral
concepts.summary: Integration by slicing the range instead of the domain. It handles far more functions and behaves well under limits.

concepts.name: Normed & Banach spaces
concepts.summary: Vector spaces with a notion of length in which Cauchy sequences converge. The main setting of functional analysis.

concepts.name: Hilbert spaces
concepts.summary: Infinite-dimensional spaces with angles and lengths. The mathematical home of quantum mechanics.

concepts.name: Fourier series
concepts.summary: Breaking a periodic signal into a sum of sine and cosine waves.

concepts.name: Fourier transform
concepts.summary: Decomposes any signal into frequencies. Used everywhere from audio to MRI scans to solving PDEs.

concepts.name: Distributions (generalised functions)
concepts.summary: Objects like the Dirac delta that behave like functions under integration, giving every function a derivative.

concepts.name: Holomorphic functions
concepts.summary: Functions of a complex variable with a complex derivative. Being differentiable once makes them infinitely smooth.

concepts.name: Cauchy's integral theorem
concepts.summary: The integral of a holomorphic function around a closed loop is zero, which makes complex analysis remarkably rigid.

concepts.name: Residue theorem
concepts.summary: Computes loop integrals from a function's behaviour at its singularities, and evaluates many real integrals as a bonus.

concepts.name: Analytic continuation
concepts.summary: A holomorphic function defined on a small region has at most one natural extension to a larger one.

concepts.name: Cauchy's integral formula
concepts.summary: The values of a holomorphic function inside a loop are determined by its values on the loop. It implies such functions are infinitely differentiable.

concepts.name: Identity theorem
concepts.summary: Two holomorphic functions that agree on a tiny region agree everywhere on a connected domain. The reason analytic continuation is unique.

concepts.name: Gamma function
concepts.summary: The continuous extension of the factorial, Γ(n) = (n − 1)!, defined for all complex numbers except the non-positive integers.

concepts.name: Poisson summation formula
concepts.summary: Summing a function over the integers equals summing its Fourier transform over the integers. A bridge between a function and its frequencies.

concepts.name: Jacobi theta function
concepts.summary: θ(t) = Σ e^(−πn²t). Poisson summation gives it a hidden symmetry under t ↦ 1/t, which Riemann used to continue the zeta function.

concepts.name: Ordinary differential equations
concepts.summary: Equations relating a function to its derivatives, describing how a system changes over time.

concepts.name: Picard–Lindelöf theorem
concepts.summary: Well-behaved differential equations have exactly one solution through each starting point.

concepts.name: Linear systems of ODEs
concepts.summary: Systems x′ = Ax are solved by the matrix exponential, with eigenvalues deciding stability.

concepts.name: Partial differential equations
concepts.summary: Equations involving derivatives in several variables, describing fields that vary in space and time.

concepts.name: Heat equation
concepts.summary: Describes how heat spreads out and smooths over time. Fourier invented his series to solve it.

concepts.name: Wave equation
concepts.summary: Describes vibrating strings, sound and light. Solutions travel at a fixed speed.

concepts.name: Navier–Stokes equations
concepts.summary: The equations of fluid flow. Whether smooth solutions always exist in 3D is a Millennium Prize problem.

concepts.name: Sobolev spaces
concepts.summary: Function spaces measuring derivatives in an averaged sense, the modern framework for solving PDEs.

concepts.name: Dynamical systems
concepts.summary: The long-term behaviour of systems that evolve by a fixed rule: fixed points, cycles and attractors.

concepts.name: Chaos
concepts.summary: Deterministic systems whose outcomes are hugely sensitive to their starting conditions, like weather.

concepts.name: Calculus of variations
concepts.summary: Finding the curve or shape that minimises a quantity, such as the shortest path or least action.

concepts.name: Ergodic theory
concepts.summary: When does a time average along one trajectory equal the average over the whole space? The mathematics of mixing.

concepts.name: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
concepts.summary: Open Millennium Prize problem: put quantum Yang–Mills theory on rigorous footing and prove its particles have positive mass.

concepts.name: Algebraic varieties
concepts.summary: The shapes cut out by systems of polynomial equations, the central objects of algebraic geometry.

concepts.name: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz
concepts.summary: A dictionary between geometry and algebra: points of a variety correspond to maximal ideals.

concepts.name: Schemes
concepts.summary: Grothendieck's generalisation of varieties that lets geometry be done over any ring, including the integers.

concepts.name: Euclidean geometry
concepts.summary: Points, lines, circles and angles, built from Euclid's postulates (made rigorous by Hilbert's axioms).

concepts.name: Pythagorean theorem
concepts.summary: In a right triangle, a² + b² = c². Perhaps the most famous theorem of all.

concepts.name: Coordinate geometry
concepts.summary: Descartes' idea: describe points by numbers so that geometry becomes algebra.

concepts.name: Conic sections
concepts.summary: Circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas: the curves made by slicing a cone, and the paths of planets.

concepts.name: Non-Euclidean geometry
concepts.summary: Geometries where the parallel postulate fails, such as the surface of a sphere or the hyperbolic plane.

concepts.name: Projective geometry
concepts.summary: Geometry with points at infinity added, so that any two lines meet. The geometry of perspective drawing.

concepts.name: Curves & surfaces
concepts.summary: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces in space: tangent lines, normal vectors and how they bend.

concepts.name: Gaussian curvature (Theorema Egregium)
concepts.summary: A surface's curvature can be measured from inside it, which is why no flat map of the Earth is perfect.

concepts.name: Smooth manifolds
concepts.summary: Spaces that look like ordinary flat space up close but can curve globally, like the surface of a sphere.

concepts.name: Differential forms
concepts.summary: Objects designed to be integrated over curves, surfaces and higher-dimensional pieces of a manifold.

concepts.name: Generalised Stokes' theorem
concepts.summary: One formula, ∫ dω = ∫ ω over the boundary, that contains the fundamental theorem of calculus and all of vector calculus.

concepts.name: Riemannian geometry
concepts.summary: Manifolds with a way to measure distance and curvature. The geometry of Einstein's general relativity.

concepts.name: Symplectic geometry
concepts.summary: The geometry of phase space in classical mechanics, where area rather than distance is preserved.

concepts.name: Gauss–Bonnet theorem
concepts.summary: Total curvature of a closed surface depends only on its number of holes, linking geometry to topology.

concepts.name: Riemann surfaces
concepts.summary: Surfaces where complex analysis works, the natural home of multi-valued functions like √z and log z.

concepts.name: Riemann–Roch theorem
concepts.summary: Counts how many functions with prescribed poles exist on a surface, using only its genus.

concepts.name: Étale cohomology
concepts.summary: Grothendieck's cohomology for varieties over any field, built to count holes where ordinary topology is unavailable.

concepts.name: Weil conjectures
concepts.summary: Point counts of varieties over finite fields obey a zeta function with its own Riemann hypothesis. Proved by Deligne in 1974.

concepts.name: Motives
concepts.summary: Grothendieck's dream of a universal cohomology from which every other cohomology theory is a shadow. Still partly conjectural.

concepts.name: Vector bundles
concepts.summary: A vector space attached to every point of a space, twisting as you move, like the tangent planes of a sphere.

concepts.name: Kähler manifolds
concepts.summary: Spaces where complex, Riemannian and symplectic geometry fit together perfectly. Most algebraic varieties are examples.

concepts.name: Hodge theory
concepts.summary: Every cohomology class has a unique harmonic representative, which splits the topology of complex spaces into finer pieces.

concepts.name: Hodge conjecture
concepts.summary: Open Millennium Prize problem: certain topological features of a projective variety are always traced out by sub-varieties.

concepts.name: Calabi–Yau manifolds
concepts.summary: Yau proved these Kähler spaces carry a metric with zero Ricci curvature. String theory uses them as its hidden dimensions.

concepts.name: Mirror symmetry
concepts.summary: Calabi–Yau spaces come in pairs where the complex geometry of one matches the symplectic geometry of the other.

concepts.name: Connections & gauge theory
concepts.summary: How to compare fibres of a bundle along a path. The mathematical form of the forces in the Standard Model.

concepts.name: Ricci flow
concepts.summary: Evolving a shape's metric like heat spreading, smoothing out its curvature over time.

concepts.name: Geometrization theorem
concepts.summary: Every closed 3-manifold splits into pieces carrying one of eight uniform geometries. Perelman's proof used Ricci flow with surgery.

concepts.name: Atiyah–Singer index theorem
concepts.summary: The number of solutions of an elliptic differential equation equals a purely topological quantity.

concepts.name: Algebraic stacks
concepts.summary: Spaces that remember the symmetries of the objects they parametrise, needed whenever objects have automorphisms.

concepts.name: Moduli of G-bundles (Bun_G)
concepts.summary: The space of all principal G-bundles on a curve. Geometric Langlands is a statement about sheaves on it.

concepts.name: ℓ-adic sheaves
concepts.summary: Sheaves in the étale world with ℓ-adic coefficients, the objects whose cohomology carries Galois representations.

concepts.name: Perverse sheaves
concepts.summary: Complexes of sheaves that behave like sheaves on singular spaces. Despite the name, they are the natural objects for intersection cohomology.

concepts.name: Decomposition theorem
concepts.summary: Beilinson, Bernstein, Deligne and Gabber: pushing forward along a proper map splits into simple perverse pieces. Its proof runs through the Weil conjectures.

concepts.name: Affine Grassmannian
concepts.summary: An infinite-dimensional space built from a reductive group and Laurent series, where local Langlands geometry happens.

concepts.name: Geometric Satake equivalence
concepts.summary: Perverse sheaves on the affine Grassmannian of G are the same as representations of its Langlands dual group. Where the dual group appears from geometry.

concepts.name: D-modules
concepts.summary: Systems of linear differential equations treated as algebraic objects on a space.

concepts.name: Riemann–Hilbert correspondence
concepts.summary: Well-behaved systems of differential equations correspond exactly to perverse sheaves. An answer to Hilbert's 21st problem.

concepts.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula
concepts.summary: Counts the points of a variety over a finite field as an alternating sum of traces on its étale cohomology.

concepts.name: Weil II (Deligne)
concepts.summary: Deligne's 1980 sequel extending the Weil conjectures from varieties to families and sheaves. The engine behind purity and the decomposition theorem.

concepts.name: Drinfeld shtukas
concepts.summary: Bundles on a curve over a finite field with a twist by Frobenius. Their moduli spaces play the role of Shimura varieties for function fields.

concepts.name: Langlands for GLₙ over function fields
concepts.summary: Laurent Lafforgue's 2002 Fields Medal work: the full global Langlands correspondence for GLₙ over function fields.

concepts.name: Langlands parameterisation (V. Lafforgue)
concepts.summary: Vincent Lafforgue (2018) attached Langlands parameters to automorphic forms for every reductive group over function fields, using geometric Satake on shtukas.

concepts.name: Sheaves
concepts.summary: A way to track data attached to open sets that can be glued from local pieces into global ones.

concepts.name: Metric spaces
concepts.summary: Sets with a distance function. Limits, continuity and completeness all make sense in them.

concepts.name: Topological spaces
concepts.summary: The most general setting for nearness and continuity, defined by which sets count as 'open'.

concepts.name: Compactness
concepts.summary: A topological version of 'finite': every open cover has a finite subcover. Compact spaces behave very well.

concepts.name: Heine–Borel theorem
concepts.summary: In ordinary space, a set is compact exactly when it is closed and bounded.

concepts.name: Connectedness
concepts.summary: A space is connected if it cannot be split into two separate open pieces.

concepts.name: Fundamental group
concepts.summary: Records the loops in a space up to continuous deformation. It detects holes, like the one in a doughnut.

concepts.name: Covering spaces
concepts.summary: Spaces that unwrap another, like a helix over a circle. They correspond to subgroups of the fundamental group.

concepts.name: Euler characteristic
concepts.summary: For any convex polyhedron, vertices − edges + faces = 2. The first topological invariant.

concepts.name: Homology
concepts.summary: Counts holes of each dimension with abelian groups. Computable, and fine enough to tell many spaces apart.

concepts.name: Cohomology
concepts.summary: A dual version of homology with a multiplication of its own, making it a sharper tool.

concepts.name: De Rham cohomology
concepts.summary: Detects the topology of a manifold using calculus: closed forms that are not derivatives reveal holes.

concepts.name: Brouwer fixed-point theorem
concepts.summary: Any continuous map from a disc to itself leaves some point fixed. Stir a cup of coffee and one point ends up where it started.

concepts.name: Knot theory
concepts.summary: Classifying knotted loops in 3D space. Knot invariants tell when two knots cannot be untangled into each other.

concepts.name: Classification of surfaces
concepts.summary: Every closed surface is a sphere with handles or cross-caps attached. Topology's first complete classification.

concepts.name: Poincaré conjecture
concepts.summary: Every simply connected closed 3-manifold is a 3-sphere. Proved by Perelman in 2003 as a consequence of geometrization.

concepts.name: Higher homotopy groups
concepts.summary: Like the fundamental group but for spheres of every dimension mapped into a space. Even for spheres themselves they are unknown in general.

concepts.name: Sheaf cohomology
concepts.summary: Measures when local solutions fail to glue into a global one. The main tool of complex and algebraic geometry.

concepts.name: Characteristic classes
concepts.summary: Cohomology classes that measure how twisted a vector bundle is, such as the Chern and Pontryagin classes.

concepts.name: Topological K-theory
concepts.summary: Turns the vector bundles over a space into an abelian group, giving a cohomology theory with remarkable periodicity.

concepts.name: Exotic spheres
concepts.summary: Milnor found 7-dimensional spheres that are topologically ordinary but cannot be smoothly reshaped into the round one.

concepts.name: Stable homotopy theory
concepts.summary: Homotopy theory after repeated suspension, where patterns settle down. Spectra are its basic objects.

concepts.name: Kervaire invariant problem
concepts.summary: Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel showed in 2009 that certain framed manifolds exist only in dimensions 2, 6, 14, 30, 62 and possibly 126.

concepts.name: Donaldson theory
concepts.summary: Uses solutions of physics equations to detect smooth structures on 4-manifolds, revealing infinitely many versions of ordinary 4D space.

concepts.name: Seiberg–Witten invariants
concepts.summary: A simpler set of equations from physics that reproduces and extends Donaldson's results on 4-manifolds.

concepts.name: Morse theory
concepts.summary: Reads off the shape of a space from the critical points of a function on it, like a landscape revealed by rising water.

concepts.name: Floer homology
concepts.summary: Morse theory on infinite-dimensional spaces, built by counting solutions of differential equations. Born from the Arnold conjecture.

concepts.name: Monopole Floer homology
concepts.summary: Kronheimer and Mrowka's Floer theory for 3-manifolds built from the Seiberg–Witten equations.

concepts.name: Heegaard Floer homology
concepts.summary: Ozsváth and Szabó's computable invariant of 3-manifolds and knots. It detects the genus of a knot and whether it is fibred.

concepts.name: Heegaard Floer = monopole Floer
concepts.summary: Two invariants with completely different definitions turn out to be isomorphic. Proved around 2010 in two independent series of long papers.

concepts.name: Counting principles
concepts.summary: The rules of sum and product for counting choices, the start of combinatorics.

concepts.name: Binomial coefficients
concepts.summary: 'n choose k' counts subsets and fills Pascal's triangle. It also expands (x + y)ⁿ.

concepts.name: Pigeonhole principle
concepts.summary: Put more than n objects into n boxes and some box holds two. Simple, and surprisingly powerful.

concepts.name: Inclusion–exclusion
concepts.summary: Count a union of sets by adding sizes, subtracting overlaps, adding back triple overlaps, and so on.

concepts.name: Recurrence relations
concepts.summary: Sequences defined by earlier terms, like the Fibonacci numbers, and methods to solve them.

concepts.name: Generating functions
concepts.summary: Packing a whole sequence into the coefficients of a power series, then using algebra to count.

concepts.name: Graphs
concepts.summary: Dots joined by lines. They model networks, maps, molecules, and this very map.

concepts.name: Trees
concepts.summary: Connected graphs with no cycles. A tree with n vertices always has n − 1 edges.

concepts.name: Eulerian paths (Königsberg bridges)
concepts.summary: A walk using every edge exactly once exists only when at most two vertices have odd degree. The founding problem of graph theory.

concepts.name: Planar graphs
concepts.summary: Graphs that can be drawn without crossings. Kuratowski's theorem pins down exactly which ones.

concepts.name: Graph colouring
concepts.summary: Colouring vertices so neighbours differ. Scheduling and register allocation are colouring problems in disguise.

concepts.name: Four colour theorem
concepts.summary: Any map can be coloured with four colours so neighbouring regions differ. The first major theorem proved by computer.

concepts.name: Ramsey theory
concepts.summary: Complete disorder is impossible: large enough structures always contain orderly patterns.

concepts.name: Matroids
concepts.summary: An abstraction of independence shared by linearly independent vectors and cycle-free sets of edges.

concepts.name: Szemerédi's theorem
concepts.summary: Any set of whole numbers with positive density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.

concepts.name: Probability
concepts.summary: Measuring chance as a number between 0 and 1, starting with dice, coins and cards.

concepts.name: Conditional probability & Bayes' theorem
concepts.summary: How to update probabilities when you learn new information. Bayes' theorem reverses the direction of a conditional.

concepts.name: Random variables
concepts.summary: Numbers whose values depend on chance, described by their distribution.

concepts.name: Expectation & variance
concepts.summary: The long-run average of a random variable, and how widely it spreads around that average.

concepts.name: Measure-theoretic probability
concepts.summary: Kolmogorov's axioms: probability as a measure of total size 1. The rigorous foundation of modern probability.

concepts.name: Normal distribution
concepts.summary: The bell curve. It shows up whenever many small independent effects add together.

concepts.name: Law of large numbers
concepts.summary: Averages of many independent trials settle down to the expected value. Why casinos always win in the long run.

concepts.name: Central limit theorem
concepts.summary: Sums of many independent random variables are approximately normally distributed, whatever the original distribution.

concepts.name: Markov chains
concepts.summary: Random processes where the next step depends only on the current state. Behind PageRank and many simulations.

concepts.name: Brownian motion
concepts.summary: The continuous random walk traced by a pollen grain in water. Its paths are continuous but nowhere differentiable.

concepts.name: Stochastic calculus
concepts.summary: Itô's calculus for integrating against randomness, used to price financial options.

concepts.name: Statistical inference
concepts.summary: Drawing conclusions about a population from a sample: estimates, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.

concepts.name: Linear regression
concepts.summary: Fitting the best straight line (or plane) through data, by orthogonal projection.

concepts.name: Bayesian inference
concepts.summary: Treating unknown quantities as random and updating beliefs about them with Bayes' theorem as data arrives.

concepts.name: Information theory
concepts.summary: Shannon's measure of information, entropy, sets the limits of data compression and reliable communication.

concepts.name: Random matrix theory
concepts.summary: The eigenvalues of large random matrices follow universal laws, seen in nuclear physics, prime numbers and wireless networks.

concepts.name: Schramm–Loewner evolution
concepts.summary: Random fractal curves driven by Brownian motion that describe the boundaries in critical physical systems.
